subject: Observability gating: per-route cost SLIs and temporary retention exception
messages:
From: Alice Johnson <alice@acme-corp.com>
To: irene_choi@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 1 Jun 2028 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Observability readiness for per-route cost SLIs

Hi Irene / Marissa,

Thanks again for the call this morning. As we prep the POC, two items are blockers for our procurement/security team signoff:

1) We need a per-route SLI for cost (p99 token cost and 7-day spend delta) so we can gate scaling to paid usage.
2) Retention for route-level telemetry: our compliance team needs 90 days of per-route cost & latency traces for sampling audits.

Currently our internal engineers can't map your route identifiers to our product routes reliably (they see an opaque path). If you can provide a short-lived mapping and an SLI definition we can use for the POC, procurement may move forward this week.

Attached: acme_poc_requirements.pdf (one-pager from compliance).

Can you confirm feasibility and an ETA for a minimal implementation? Ideally we need something to validate by next Friday 2028-06-09.

Best,
Alice
Senior Platform PM, Acme Corp

---

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Alice Johnson <alice@acme-corp.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, dylan_brooks@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 1 Jun 2028 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability readiness for per-route cost SLIs

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear ask and the doc.

Short answer: feasible, with two pragmatic constraints we want to call out up front.

What we can do this week (MVP):
- Provide a temporary route-ID mapping table that maps Redwood’s endpoint paths to Acme’s product route names (CSV). This will be a one-off export we can host on a shared Drive link for the POC.
- Ship an SLI definition for per-route cost: p99 per-token cost (USD) computed daily + 7d rolling spend delta alert. We’ll also provide a JSON schema for the metric so your ingestion can consume it.

Constraints / exception request:
- 90d retention of full per-route traces (span-level traces and per-token payload metadata) is heavier than our standard 30d retention for route-level telemetry. For a short-term POC we can grant a 60d retention exception for the per-route aggregated metrics (not raw payloads); keeping raw traces for 90d would need an enterprise data-add-on.

Next steps I propose:
1) We’ll put together the mapping CSV + the SLI spec by EOD Monday 2028-06-04.
2) Marissa (cc) will outline the ingestion contract and a fallback mapping if some route IDs are batched.
3) Dylan / Soojin will scope a 60d retention configuration and any security controls required for longer retention.

I’ll attach a short checklist so we can get procurement what they need quickly.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with the Drive link once the mapping is ready.

Cheers,
Irene Choi
Director, Observability Product
Redwood Inference

Attachment: irene_obs-gating-checklist.md

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Observability readiness for per-route cost SLIs

Thanks — quick technical notes and a proposed fallback so the POC isn’t blocked if some routes are opaque:

1) Mapping approach: we’ll produce CSV with columns (redwood_route_id, redwood_path_pattern, acme_route_name). For any route patterns that are heavily parameterized we’ll include a normalized pattern (e.g., /checkout/{flow}/confirm) rather than raw IDs.

2) SLI spec (MVP):
- metric_name: route.cost_per_token_p99_daily
- labels: {route_name, region, model_family}
- calculation: daily p99( token_cost_per_request ) aggregated across requests with label route_name
- alert: if 7d rolling spend delta > 25% AND p99_cost > $0.10 for two consecutive days -> create PagerDuty incident to Redwood ops channel

3) Retention exception scope:
- We can grant a 60d retention for aggregated per-route metrics and 30d for span-level traces for the POC.
- If Acme needs 90d for audits, that requires: (a) a signed data-addendum, (b) enabling encrypted long-term metric buckets, and (c) approval from security and finance (cost impact).

4) Short-term fallback: if the mapping CSV misses some route IDs the agent will emit a synthetic label "unknown_route_bucket" we can sum and later reconcile. I’ll attach a sample mapping CSV and a reconciliation playbook.

Attached: marissa_proposed-mapping.csv (sample), reconciliation_playbook.md

If that sounds reasonable I’ll open a small internal JIRA to track the exception approval and the data-addendum ask. We can meet Wed morning to walk through the SLI JSON.

—Marissa
Product Lead, Observability
Redwood Inference
